title: FCA: convention checking + suppressions
description:
## Parent

sutra/v1/5 — PRD: sutra v1 review intelligence engine

## What to build

Add convention violation checking to the FCA engine. Given a set of changed symbols, check them against active conventions and return violations. Parse `.sutra/rules.toml` `[conventions]` section for suppressions (by stable hash) and per-symbol exemptions. Extend the rules.toml parser introduced by the forbidden deps slice.

Example config:
```toml
[conventions]
suppress = ["a1b4c2d1"]

[[conventions.exempt]]
convention = "e5f6g7h8"
symbols = ["InternalError"]
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `check(symbols) -> Vec<Violation>` returns convention violations for changed symbols
- [ ] Suppressed conventions (by hash) produce no violations
- [ ] Per-symbol exemptions work correctly
- [ ] Convention violations are distinct type from DD constraint violations
- [ ] `.sutra/rules.toml` `[conventions]` section parsed correctly
- [ ] Tests: violation detection, suppression, exemption, no false positives on unchanged code

## Blocked by

- sutra/v1/10 — DD: forbidden deps + rules.toml (rules.toml parser)
- sutra/v1/11 — FCA: convention extraction + persistence

messages.text:
Codex review: needs-attention.

[medium] Per-symbol exemptions match on `sym.name` (qualified_name) which isn't globally unique — two symbols named `process` in different files would both be exempted if one is listed. ConventionViolation also lacks file/id context for downstream disambiguation.

Recommendation: carry file-qualified identity through FCA checking and match exemptions against that. Include in ConventionViolation for downstream sutra_review integration.
